C# targets `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` (CombatState.cs:142), and IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(CombatState, this)` (Creature.cs:285-299). The sim's Relic.living_enemies() (relics/base.py:447) filters on `not e.is_gone` ONLY -- its own docstring concedes the should_allow_hitting predicate is applied by DamageCmd rather than here, and PowerCmd.apply does not apply it either (that absence is audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json gap G6, the missing CanReceivePowers backstop). So an alive-but-unhittable enemy receives Vulnerable in the sim and is skipped by C#. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30 round 11 -- the census now has three members, not one): `grep -n 'def should_allow_hitting' sts2_rl/powers.py` finds IllusionPower (powers.py:1908), the Decimillipede segment's ReattachPower (powers.py:2780) and AdaptablePower (powers.py:3905) -- all three gate on their own `is_reviving` flag, set only inside `on_death` after the creature has already taken a lethal hit once, which cannot be true during turn 1's setup, the only turn Bag of Marbles fires. Porting a turn-1 untargetable enemy, or any effect that makes a creature unhittable before the first player turn, makes it live. Distinct from power_cmd G6: that gap is the missing backstop INSIDE PowerCmd.apply, this one is the wrong enemy set at the CALL site, and fixing either alone would leave the other.
